# Website Studio Design & Functionality System

Version: STUDIO_CLAUDE_CRAFT_V1 — approved-example extraction, Nov 7, 2026 (PST).
This is an instruction/playbook, not model training. Future Naive sessions must use this system and verify outputs; it does not guarantee Claude-identical results.

## 1. Source of truth and business state

Approved reference implementations are demos/deploy/studio/{don-dar,azimut,sciencely,fine-cup}/index.html. These four self-contained HTML files were approved in the local STATUS.md and deployed byte-for-byte to the existing personal-site app on Nov 7, 2026 at 3:43 PM PST. The deployment is apd_ptkynv2ts7qb748031eahyekwd.
Stable base: https://personal-site-xs12r15q0hxw.vercel.app . Use /studio/<slug>/; do not request a new URL after each deploy.
There are FOUR showcase pages, not four selected prospects. CRM currently has THREE selected clients: Don-Dar, Azimut, Fine Cup. Sciencely remains a visual example only: chosen=false, status=researched, outreach_status=not_started, with a dropped/franchise note. Do not revive that sales lead without explicit approval. A maximum of four client packets is a ceiling, not a reason to invent a fourth lead or restart research.

## 2. Research -> art direction -> complete implementation

1. Identify the real business category, audience, market/languages and one visitor task (compare rooms, request a trip program, compare science programs, inspect cafe stock). Read the business's own site. Save exact evidence URLs and short excerpts; distinguish observation, inference and unverified fact.
2. Actually study 3–5 strong real sites in that category. Record URLs, the date, and a specific transferable lesson for typography, information hierarchy, navigation, product presentation and conversion. Never claim reference research you did not perform; if blocked, report the limitation.
3. Write a compact art-direction brief BEFORE markup: two-font pairing, 4–6 color roles, one original category motif, mobile hero composition, section sequence, primary/secondary CTA, and the functional problem being solved. Different businesses must not be one template recolored.
4. Build complete, production-quality frontend HTML/CSS with minimal vanilla JS when sufficient. Inline CSS, custom properties, semantic landmarks and native controls are the proven baseline here; no framework/build complexity merely for show. The demo behavior can be complete locally without pretending the backend is live.
5. Populate useful, dense category content. Lead with what customers need, not generic feature cards. Reference craft, never pixel-clone; do not copy logos, photos, branded artwork or marketing prose. Use original CSS/SVG illustrations and typographic wordmarks, with captions identifying drawings as illustrations rather than the business's premises/products.
6. Test mobile, desktop and keyboard use, local form behavior and provenance. Save source, references.md, evidence notes, screenshots and a machine-readable verification report. Fix actual failures before one scoped deploy. Stop at the authorized scope and budget; report blockers rather than buying tools or starting more agents.

## 3. Four distinct approved identities

### Don-Dar — quiet boutique / editorial room index
- Cormorant Garamond 500/600 + Manrope 400–700. Ivory #f6f1e7, paper #fbf8f1, navy #1d2a3a, night #16212e, muted brass #a8834a / #c8a96e; sage accent.
- Generous ivory space, thin rules, letterspaced small labels, expressive italic serif emphasis. Original arched dusk-window SVG; stylized orientation diagram, explicitly not a scale map.
- Hero: “Quiet rooms, an honest page, a park at the door.” Asymmetric desktop text/art split, compact art on mobile; primary rooms/rates CTA and secondary dates enquiry.
- Page: disclosure -> masthead -> hero -> evidence/standfirst -> section chips -> numbered room/rate catalogue (2 columns on desktop) -> neighbourhood list + diagram -> native FAQ -> dates/guests/room enquiry preview -> disclosure footer. All example rates, dimensions/features and FAQ answers are labeled pending confirmation. No booking or availability engine.

### Azimut — alpine field guide / route catalogue
- Big Shoulders Display 700–900 + Inter 400–700. Pine #1f3a2e, deep #13241c, glacier #cfe3ea, snow #f5f6f1, ember #e8642c, paper #f1efe6.
- Condensed uppercase display type, trail-marker shapes, full-width mountain panel, original layered ridgelines and contour diagram; glacier itinerary sheet, orange accents and a cut-ridge footer. Inter here is an intentional quiet supporting face, NOT a generic default art direction.
- Hero: “Canyons, lakes, and a plan in writing.” Primary trip index, secondary request current program.
- Page: disclosure -> mountain hero -> promise/evidence -> section chips -> coded trips with grades, duration, pace and sample figures -> grade legend/diagram -> illustrative day-by-day itinerary with included/excluded rows -> observed pipe-valve-template problem -> draft FAQ -> traveller-specific preview form -> footer. Route details, costs and FAQ drafts stay caveated; no countdowns or invented availability.

### Sciencely — playful lab notebook / protocol cards
- Fredoka 500–700 + Nunito 400–800. Navy ink #1b2a4a, warm paper #fbfaf4, graph grid #e3ecf3, teal #13a8a0, pink #ff5d8f, yellow #ffc93c; small violet accent #7b61ff.
- 24px graph paper, outlined rounded stickers, hard offset shadows, original flask/test-tube/atom SVG, playful highlighted words, slightly offset protocol cards. This is a category-appropriate illustration system, not a SaaS gradient.
- Hero: “Every big discovery starts with «А почему?»” Primary program cards and secondary current-program enquiry.
- Page: disclosure -> masthead/hero -> sourced-format summary -> section chips -> protocol cards (age/format/duration/sample price) -> question/experiment/explanation method -> broken-price/language problem -> parents' FAQ -> local sign-up preview -> footer. No identifiable children or child photos without guardian consent. This remains a showcase, NOT an active prospect.

### Fine Cup — warm roastery / functional menu board
- DM Serif Display + Work Sans 400–700. Espresso #24160f, roast #3b2418, crema #f2e3cc, cream #faf4ea, milk #fffdf8, terracotta #c4613a, caramel #d9a066.
- Dark roast hero, original steaming-cup/bean SVG, restrained steam animation, typographic menu boards, tilted stock stamps, receipt-shaped ticket. Sourced short quotation in the example is attributed evidence, not permission to reuse marketing copy for future clients.
- Hero: “Freshly roasted, straight into the cup.” Primary menu/stock, secondary local order builder.
- Page: disclosure -> roastery hero -> evidence -> chips -> dated-snapshot panel/download -> JS-rendered Coffee/Bakery/Retail boards -> honest stock legend -> explicitly unverified sample hours -> observed EN cafe-information gap -> checkbox order builder + live total/receipt -> footer.
- Exact demo behavior: 8 embedded rows, change event recomputes a one-of-each selected-item total in AZN; sold-out croissant disabled. aria-live=polite ticket; no customer name/phone/email fields. Collection/time selects are illustrative controls, not fulfilment. Submit reveals “nothing was sent”; it does not reserve/decrement inventory or send an order. No payment, persistence or live DB read.

## 4. Shared implementation grammar

- Mobile-first: banner, business identity, concise benefit/task headline and clear primary action high on the page. Mobile art is short (about 150–190px); desktop composition expands at min-width:760px. Use 1120–1140px max-width wrappers, 20px mobile / 32px desktop gutters, generous ~56px section starts, readable text widths ~64–72ch.
- Fluid clamp() type, left-aligned task-led copy, one dominant action and a visually quiet alternative. Draw useful catalogues, itineraries, menu boards and FAQs instead of repeating empty three-column icon-card sections. Genuine three-route/program catalogues are fine; identical decorative feature grids across every business are not.
- Horizontal, overflow-scroll section-chip nav on phones (no nonworking hamburger), anchors to actual IDs, official-site links and preserved draft promo links where available. Native details/summary FAQ, explicit input labels, semantic article/section/header/footer, correct lang, descriptive aria-labels for meaningful drawings and aria-hidden for decoration.
- Touch controls about 48–52px high, visible focus, 16px inputs to avoid iOS zoom; responsive one-column layouts that become purposeful two-/three-column content at desktop. Reduced-motion CSS disables smooth scroll/transitions; Fine Cup also disables animation. Check contrast and focus rather than assuming the examples are fully audited.
- Required demo behavior: form submit prevents default; show an on-page “Demo only — nothing was sent” confirmation. No request, mailto/WhatsApp send link, analytics capture, localStorage, sessionStorage or PII persistence. Google font downloads are styling requests; “no network request” describes submission behavior, not font loading. Local forms may accept sample input in memory only; use synthetic test data.
- Stock: source can be a dated static SQL snapshot when live reads are unavailable. Label provenance/time, illustrative status and NOT LIVE next to data; publish credential-free JSON. State rules: stock=0 Sold out, stock<=2 Out soon, then stock<=low_stock_threshold Running low, otherwise Available. Existing Fine Cup labels are precomputed in the embedded rows and rendered from stock_label; they happen to match those rules. Future implementations should derive/validate labels from numeric fields, disable sold-out selection, recompute totals and test boundary values. Never invent predictive run-out times without velocity data.
- Language pills in the approved examples say “trilingual-ready” or “bilingual-ready”; they are NOT working language switches. Never report real AZ/RU/EN localization unless translations and routing/toggling are actually implemented and tested. Native date fields do not equal a complete booking engine; add check-out-after-check-in validation for a real product. Empty-order validation, stale-stock handling, loading/errors and server-side business validation are separate production requirements.

## 5. Safety, originality and evidence

Every page visibly and persistently says “Proposed redesign for [business] — demo, not the official website.” Include noindex and a footer reiteration. All unverified prices, hours, room dimensions, route grades, program ages/durations, FAQ policies and stock must be labeled sample/illustrative/pending confirmation. Never invent awards, testimonials, customer metrics, availability, business contact details, affiliations or performance claims. A public preview is published as a DEMO; the examples' phrase “unpublished draft” means unapproved proposal, not that the URL is private.
No copied logos/photos/domain impersonation; no unlicensed fandom merchandise. No contact-list blasts. Prefer AZ/KZ at equal fit. Draft outreach only; founder/client approval before any external send or client launch. CEO email.send and social.post must remain ask; designer remains deny. No MobileRun DMs/comments/posts or business-account login. Never put secrets/connection strings in prompts, HTML, JSON, archives or logs. MCP auth uses sanctioned vault injection, not inline Authorization headers. If a tool is absent, report it; local .env presence is not agent access.
Avoid thoughtless Inter/Poppins/Roboto defaults, purple/indigo SaaS gradients, mesh backgrounds, centered-everything heroes, glassmorphism as the visual concept, emoji-as-icons, generic Unsplash and “unlock your potential” filler. Do not overfit this into a blanket ban on every gradient, grid or neutral body font: original landscape/coffee illustration shading and meaningful catalogue grids are demonstrated exceptions. Prefer drawn SVG/real text to decorative symbols for future icons.

## 6. Non-destructive deployment contract

Existing app personal-site (app_9d9wf8023mvy8vayht3x0gpjnc), frontend_only; Naive owns its Vercel project. Stable base stays unchanged. Always use SDK apps.get/deployments/deploymentFiles to retrieve the CURRENT ready full file map; stage a complete merge; overlay ONLY authorized paths. Preserve every other path byte-for-byte including index.html, style.css, photo/, studio/index.html, studio/promo/*, studio/assets/*, inventory JSON, references and archives. If export is incomplete or another deployment landed since the read, STOP/refetch; never reconstruct the whole app from four public pages. apps.deploy expects file values encoded base64, including binary assets; preserve the existing encoding of untouched entries.
Check protected-file hashes before upload and re-fetch the deployed tree to prove all non-target entries stayed identical. Wait for ready, then GET stable routes and compare bytes/hash/title and distinctive content, not status 200 alone. Verify homepage, studio index, promos and snapshot still work. Save deployment ID, PST time and evidence; the optional preview URL is not a replacement for the stable URL. Do not create a replacement app or change DNS. No concurrent deployers; site-editor/personal CEO are out of studio scope. Prompt rules alone do not prevent another agent overwriting /studio: enforce single-writer ownership/deploy-lock or a scoped merge gateway before claiming autonomous safety.

## 7. Definition updates are not a running company

Persist this system inside both studio agent definitions as well as local prompts; a laptop file alone is not available in a Naive sandbox. Definition edits version the prompt but do not train a model, wake idle runs or update sessions pinned to old versions. Never run npm run ceo, run-ceo.ts, launch-designer.mjs or sessions.create/send just to save a prompt. No new sessions, schedules, paid plans, top-ups or budget increases as part of teaching. A later explicitly approved evaluation should use the new version and a bounded brief, not a fresh discovery loop.

## 8. Release checklist and handover

Report pass/fail with artifacts for: factual provenance and sample labels; independent category identity; complete customer-task flow; mobile widths 360/390 and desktop 1440 with no accidental horizontal body overflow; nav/CTA/FAQ and keyboard; focus/contrast/reduced motion; local-submit network interception proving zero submission/persistence; Fine Cup stock boundaries/disabled sold-out/total; live-response hash; protected routes unchanged; durable source and CRM state; spend and blockers.
Persist researched businesses and demo/outreach/ops status in Neon businesses through sanctioned tools. If inaccessible, save a labeled crm-snapshot.json and report UNSYNCED rather than falsely claiming a DB write. A full autonomous product additionally needs an authorized intake and bounded run trigger, persistent job/state/artifact storage, tested read/write credentials, a safe deployment owner, QA/fix/release loop, monitoring/rollback and explicit approval lanes for outreach, paid actions and client production activation. Do not enable any of those merely because this playbook lists them.

## 9. Original first websites and bounded learning — STUDIO_CREW_V2

There are TWO equally valid tracks: redesign an existing website, or create an original first proposed website for a business whose presence is social/listing-only. For the latter, do not invent a broken website or imply an official relationship. Record dated search queries, exact listing/social URLs and short evidence excerpts. Say “No independent website found in these checked sources,” not a universal proof of absence. Check the business name + city + website, listing website fields and public profile links. Reject ambiguous identities, chains/franchises and businesses where evidence is too weak. Prefer Azerbaijan/Kazakhstan.

For original sites, use “Proposed first website for [business] — demo, not the official website” in a persistent banner plus noindex/footer. Separate sourced facts, design inferences, illustrative content and owner-confirmation-needed fields. Omit unverifiable contacts and addresses; never fabricate awards, reviews, testimonials, hours, prices or bookings. Samples must be adjacent-labeled. Build one complete local visitor task, with no submission requests, sending links, analytics, storage or PII persistence. Study 3–5 actual category references and create an independent identity, not a copy of the four showcases.

Four-person crew only: website-studio-ceo coordinates; scout researches; designer builds; QA verifies. CEO alone accesses Neon/MobileRun and deploys. Workers do not delegate, deploy, create agents/sessions, modify agent definitions, buy anything or send anything. One bounded coordinator run may call each listed teammate once, plus at most one same-thread QA repair; no recursive session spawning or schedules. Human approval is always needed for outreach, purchases and client production activation.

QA returns pass/fail evidence, not assertions, at mobile 360/390 and desktop 1440, keyboard, local forms and protected hashes. If browser verification is unavailable, mark NOT TESTED and do not claim a full QA pass. QA writes three actionable lessons per page (observation -> general rule -> verification test). CEO appends lessons to a durable website-studio-lessons Naive skill version or scoped page artifact under the new demo path; future runs must read the latest lessons before briefing. Lessons do not grant authority to rewrite prompts, expand budgets or spawn a loop.

Deployment is single-writer CEO, current full map -> complete merge -> protected-file hash comparison -> apps.deploy base64 -> ready -> live-byte check. No partial-map replacement. Only authorized new studio slug files and optional studio index card may change. Preserve all four Claude pages, homepage, promos, assets and unrelated routes. If export/locking/verification fails, save artifacts and STOP rather than deploy unsafely. Research via Neon must inspect current businesses schema and make non-destructive inserts/updates only; do not delete/change existing clients or revive Sciencely. Report UNSYNCED with an exact error when tools fail.

ejickmini — Murad's personal site. One page, plain HTML/CSS, no build, no JS. Dark design; interaction is CSS-only (hover, marquee, details, scroll reveal).

A profile page for Murad — Chemical Engineer with a background in startups and

contact info.

Static files only, served as-is. No framework, no build step, no tracking scripts.

Follow the `naive/personal-site` skill:

   `height` set.
4. `apps deploy` with `dir: "./personal-site"`.

Never invent a fact about Murad — only use what he has given directly.
